definitions.explanation: The upper portion or top area of something. Used in both everyday descriptions and technical contexts to indicate the part that is higher in position.

examples.japanese: ページの{上部|じょうぶ}にロゴがある。
examples.english: There is a logo at the top of the page.

examples.japanese: {棚|たな}の{上部|じょうぶ}に{本|ほん}を{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: I lined up books on the upper part of the shelf.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}の{上部|じょうぶ}には{展望|てんぼう}デッキが{設|もう}けられている。
examples.english: An observation deck is installed in the upper part of this building.

notes:
USAGE: {上部|じょうぶ} refers to the physical upper portion of an object, structure, or space. It is somewhat formal and is common in written descriptions, instructions, and technical texts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上部|じょうぶ}に{位置|いち}する (to be located in the upper part)
- {画面|がめん}の{上部|じょうぶ} (the top of the screen)
- {胸|むね}の{上部|じょうぶ} (the upper chest)

NOTE: Do not confuse with {丈夫|じょうぶ} (sturdy, durable), which has the same reading but a completely different meaning.

PAIR: The opposite is {下部|かぶ} (lower part).
